newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stock exchange hits year low.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stock exchange hits year low.

text.p: Shares on Cyprus's stock exchange inched lower on Friday, closing the week with total losses of 1.28 percent.

The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) all-share index closed at 79.67, its lowest point this year. Last week the CSE index closed at 80.71 points in weak trade sparked by renewed tension between Cyprus and Turkey over the island's plans to deploy anti-aircraft missiles and Turkish threats they would destroy them.
"I think that has blown over," said Christodoulos Ellinas of Share Link Stockbrokers in Nicosia.
"We will start seeing positive effects on the market once banks clarify their intentions as regards interest rates," he added.
Effective Friday, the central bank cut its lombard lending rate by half a percentage point to 7.0 percent and cut its overnight deposit rate to 4.0 percent from 5.0 percent.

The move is widely seen as the central bank's go-ahead to commercial banks to lower their own rates to the public without the need for a special directive, a move which is expected to enhance investor activity on the CSE.

The central bank expects commercial banks to follow suit with reductions in their retail rates, now 8.5 percent for loans and 7.0 percent for deposits, central bank governor Afxentis Afxentiou said on Thursday.
Banks had not announced any changes in their retail interest rate policy by late Friday. Bank representatives said they were still studying the effects of the central bank rate cut.

The banking stocks index closed at 89.74 points, slightly lower than 89.87 registered last week. Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus lost one cent to close at 335.5. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 325, up half a cent from last week. The Hellenic Bank dropped half a cent to 259. Universal Savings Bank gained half a cent, closing at 137.5.
Insurance stocks closed at 56.05 points, down 0.22 points from last Friday. Universal Life made gains of nine cents, closing at 372.5.
Paneuropean Insurance declined 4 cents, closing at 114.5.
The best performer of the week was Liberty Life Insurance which jumped 22.5 cents to close on Friday at 104.5.
Shares on Liberty Life were suspended for the first three trading days of the week after it charged Paneuropean with making an unfriendly takeover bid.

Paneuropean announced on Monday it purchased 262,740 shares in Liberty at 95 cents a share, giving it a 25 percent stake in the company. Liberty objected to the wording of the announcement, and Paneuropean subsequently removed the clause relating to the percentage represented by its shareholding.

National carrier Cyprus Airways fell to an all-time low of 31.1 cents from 35.5 last Friday. Earlier this week its newly appointed chairman Takis Kyriakides said the airline would have an "expiry date" if it is not restructured soon.
Cement producer Vassiliko retreated 8 cents, closing at 153. Beer and wine producers Keo inched up half a cent to 110.5.
